title: Literature-backed mechanisms for intraday and short swing idea generation

out_of_scope: Strategic portfolio allocation and long-horizon asset pricing
Monthly or annual factor portfolios without a short-horizon transmission mechanism
News sentiment as a standalone signal

mechanisms.title: Order-flow imbalance relative to displayed depth
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Over short intervals, additions, cancellations and aggressive executions alter the balance of supplied liquidity; the price response depends on imbalance relative to depth.
expected_actions: Consume, cancel, replenish or reprice displayed liquidity as imbalance changes

observable_signatures.statement: Signed order-flow imbalance normalized by contemporaneous displayed depth
Persistent imbalance between best bid and ask queues before the next mid-price change

phases.trigger: Depth-normalized order-flow imbalance becomes extreme
phases.expected_response: The next short-horizon mid-price change is more likely in the direction of the imbalance

phases.trigger: Extreme signed flow persists while the mid-price barely moves
phases.expected_response: Passive replenishment or hidden liquidity absorbs the flow and changes the subsequent response path

phases.trigger: Previously persistent imbalance decays or reverses
phases.expected_response: Continuation weakens or the price partially retraces as pressure ends

alternative_observables.observable: Replenishment rate at the depleted best quote
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether replenishment, rather than price direction, identifies absorption and predicts whether the next imbalance produces continuation.

violation_hypotheses: A missing price response despite extreme imbalance may reveal hidden or rapidly replenished liquidity; exhaustion of that absorber may predict a delayed move.

literature_sources.citation: Cont, Kukanov and Stoikov (2014), The Price Impact of Order Book Events, Journal of Financial Econometrics 12(1), 47-88.
literature_sources.supports: Short-interval price changes are strongly related to order-flow imbalance, with impact inversely related to depth.

literature_sources.citation: Gould and Bonart (2016), Queue Imbalance as a One-Tick-Ahead Price Predictor.
literature_sources.supports: Queue imbalance contains information about the direction of the next mid-price movement, particularly for large-tick stocks.

mechanisms.title: Incremental execution of large hidden orders
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: A large parent order cannot be executed immediately without excessive impact, so it is split into a persistent sequence of child orders whose impact grows during execution and partially reverts afterward.
constraints_or_rules: A large desired position change must be spread across time to limit impact and information leakage
expected_actions: Submit correlated same-sign child orders at a participation rate linked to market activity

observable_signatures.statement: Persistent same-sign trade flow and autocorrelated initiator direction
Concave price impact that grows while the inferred execution remains active

phases.trigger: A persistent same-sign flow episode begins
phases.expected_response: Price impact continues in the direction of the inferred parent order while participation remains elevated

phases.trigger: Same-sign persistence and participation fall toward baseline
phases.expected_response: Directional impact stops accumulating as the inferred parent order completes

phases.trigger: The inferred metaorder ends
phases.expected_response: A temporary component of peak impact partially reverts

alternative_observables.observable: Participation rate and child-order timing rather than repeated identical print size
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether persistent participation relative to market volume is a better footprint than exact periodicity or block-size repetition.

violation_hypotheses: Persistent same-sign flow without impact may indicate strategic passive execution or a competing metaorder; the eventual imbalance of participation rates may be the tradable state.

literature_sources.citation: Moro et al. (2009), Market impact and trading profile of hidden orders in stock markets, Physical Review E 80, 066102.
literature_sources.supports: Reconstructed hidden orders are executed incrementally; impact grows during execution and partially reverts after completion.

mechanisms.title: Intermediary inventory pressure and mean reversion
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Risk-averse intermediaries absorb asynchronous investor demand and use temporary price concessions to attract offsetting flow and mean-revert inventory.
constraints_or_rules: Intermediaries have finite risk capacity and seek to reduce unwanted inventory
expected_actions: Adjust prices, trade timing or supplied liquidity to induce offsetting demand

observable_signatures.statement: Return in the direction of a non-informational imbalance followed by partial reversal
Price pressure transmitted to correlated instruments through shared risk-bearing capacity

phases.trigger: A large imbalance reaches constrained intermediaries
phases.expected_response: A temporary price concession develops while intermediaries absorb inventory

phases.trigger: Offsetting demand arrives and intermediary inventory normalizes
phases.expected_response: The temporary component of price pressure mean-reverts

alternative_observables.observable: Cross-instrument pressure conditional on return correlation
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether a large imbalance in one instrument predicts a temporary move and reversal in correlated instruments that share liquidity providers.

violation_hypotheses: Price continuation instead of reversal may indicate informed flow or insufficient intermediary capacity rather than temporary inventory pressure.

literature_sources.citation: Hendershott and Menkveld (2014), Price Pressures, Journal of Financial Economics 114(3), 405-423.
literature_sources.supports: A dynamic intermediary inventory model and data imply temporary price pressure with inventory mean reversion at roughly a one-day scale.

mechanisms.title: Stop-loss and take-profit clustering around salient levels
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Stop-loss and take-profit orders cluster around salient price levels; reaching or crossing those levels changes the composition and urgency of executable flow.
actors: Traders using conditional stop-loss or take-profit orders
constraints_or_rules: Conditional orders become executable when specified price levels are reached
expected_actions: Trigger urgent same-direction stop flow beyond clustered levels and offsetting take-profit flow near levels

observable_signatures.statement: Acceleration after crossing a salient round-number region
Opposing flow and reversal near a level where take-profit orders cluster

phases.trigger: Price approaches a salient level from one side
phases.expected_response: Take-profit flow can slow or reverse the approach before the stop region is crossed

phases.trigger: Price crosses beyond the salient level into the stop region
phases.expected_response: Urgent stop execution accelerates the move beyond its pre-crossing rate

phases.trigger: Triggered stop flow decays after the level crossing
phases.expected_response: Acceleration fades and a temporary overshoot may retrace

alternative_observables.observable: Change in trade arrival intensity immediately before and after the crossing
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether arrival-intensity discontinuity around the level is more stable than the raw return pattern.

violation_hypotheses: A level crossing without acceleration may indicate that stops were already depleted or absorbed; the absence of the expected cascade may predict reversal.

literature_sources.citation: Osler (2003), Currency Orders and Exchange Rate Dynamics, Journal of Finance 58(5), 1791-1819.
literature_sources.supports: Currency stop-loss and take-profit orders cluster around round numbers and can explain acceleration after crossings and reversals near levels.

mechanisms.title: Delta hedging under short or long gamma exposure
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Option and leveraged-product hedgers adjust underlying exposure as price and time change; short-gamma hedging trades with the move while long-gamma hedging can trade against it.
constraints_or_rules: Delta exposure changes mechanically with the underlying price, volatility and time to expiry
expected_actions: Buy or sell the underlying or a linked future to restore target hedge exposure

observable_signatures.statement: Continuation into the final part of the session when hedgers are plausibly short gamma
Price and volume response across option, future and underlying markets as hedge demand changes

phases.trigger: A directional move changes estimated net hedge demand materially
phases.expected_response: Short-gamma hedging reinforces the move while long-gamma hedging dampens it

phases.trigger: Hedge adjustment is executed in a linked future or ETF
phases.expected_response: The hedge instrument moves first and transmits pressure to the cash basket or underlying

phases.trigger: The hedging need falls after expiry, close or a reversal in the underlying
phases.expected_response: Reinforcing pressure weakens and part of the move can reverse over subsequent sessions

alternative_observables.observable: Difference between late-session realized sensitivity in negative- and positive-gamma states
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test a state interaction in continuation or volatility rather than relying on an unconditional directional signal.

violation_hypotheses: A strong directional move without the expected gamma-state response may reveal offsetting auction, index or discretionary flow, or that hedging occurs in another linked instrument.

literature_sources.citation: Baltussen et al. (2021), Hedging Demand and Market Intraday Momentum, Journal of Financial Economics 142(1), 377-403.
literature_sources.supports: Late-session intraday momentum across futures is linked to gamma hedging demand from options and leveraged products.

mechanisms.title: Underlying-price pressure near option strikes at expiration
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Near option expiration, hedge rebalancing and strategic trading can concentrate underlying prices around option strike levels.
constraints_or_rules: Expiration fixes exercise and settlement relevance around discrete strike prices
expected_actions: Rebalance hedges or trade the underlying as spot approaches economically important strikes

observable_signatures.statement: Closing prices of optionable underlyings cluster near listed strikes on expiration dates

phases.trigger: Expiration approaches with spot near a strike carrying material option interest
phases.expected_response: Hedge sensitivity and strategic interest increase as distance to the strike shrinks

phases.trigger: The underlying trades near the strike into the expiration close
phases.expected_response: Underlying-price pressure or clustering around the strike becomes stronger

phases.trigger: Expiration and associated settlement complete
phases.expected_response: Strike-related pressure disappears and any temporary component can release

alternative_observables.observable: Closing-distance change to the nearest high-interest strike
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether distance compression, not raw return direction, intensifies in the final interval on expiration days.

violation_hypotheses: Failure to cluster near a seemingly important strike may identify insufficient dealer exposure, dominant fundamental flow or an incorrect proxy for economically active open interest.

literature_sources.citation: Ni, Pearson and Poteshman (2005), Stock Price Clustering on Option Expiration Dates, Journal of Financial Economics 78(1), 49-87.
literature_sources.supports: Optionable stocks cluster near strike prices on expiration dates, with evidence for hedge rebalancing and proprietary trading.

mechanisms.title: Predictable futures-roll flow and strategic liquidity provision
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: A fund or index that follows a public roll schedule must transfer exposure between expiries; strategic traders can anticipate, absorb and redistribute that pressure across contracts and days.
constraints_or_rules: Exposure must be moved from an expiring contract to a later contract on a known schedule
expected_actions: Sell one expiry and buy another while liquidity providers pre-position and later unwind

observable_signatures.statement: Temporary pressure in the calendar spread around the announced roll window
Increased strategic liquidity provision and rapid replenishment during a predictable roll

phases.trigger: A public roll date approaches
phases.expected_response: Strategic traders position ahead of the known directional spread flow

phases.trigger: The scheduled roll executes
phases.expected_response: Additional liquidity providers absorb the predictable flow and compress its immediate impact

phases.trigger: The scheduled roll flow ends
phases.expected_response: Temporary spread pressure reverses as strategic positions are offloaded

alternative_observables.observable: Resiliency time of each expiry after an order imbalance
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether predictable roll days change resiliency and liquidity provision rather than simply causing a directional futures return.

violation_hypotheses: No raw price pressure during a predictable roll may indicate successful sunshine liquidity; the opportunity may move to pre-positioning, spread resiliency or the post-roll unwind.

literature_sources.citation: Bessembinder et al. (2016), Liquidity, Resiliency and Market Quality around Predictable Trades, Journal of Financial Economics 121(1), 142-166.
literature_sources.supports: Strategic traders anticipate a large predictable USO roll; temporary impact reverses rapidly and liquidity can improve on roll days.

mechanisms.title: Closing-auction imbalance, absorption and reversal
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Benchmarking and end-of-day execution concentrate volume in the closing auction; published imbalance information attracts liquidity and creates phase-specific price impact and later reversal.
constraints_or_rules: Closing auctions publish indicative prices or imbalances and produce the official closing price
expected_actions: Submit, cancel or offset auction interest as imbalance information evolves

observable_signatures.statement: Time series of published imbalance, indicative match price, paired volume and reference price before the close
Auction price impact conditional on imbalance and available offsetting depth

phases.trigger: A material closing imbalance is disseminated before the auction
phases.expected_response: Liquidity providers and anticipatory traders adjust continuous-book and auction orders before the cross

phases.trigger: The closing auction clears
phases.expected_response: The clearing price reflects imbalance relative to auction depth and market-design rules

phases.trigger: The market reopens after a closing auction with a large temporary component
phases.expected_response: Temporary auction impact dissipates over following sessions

alternative_observables.observable: Revision path of indicative price and paired volume
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether improving versus worsening imbalance revisions predict the final auction displacement more directly than the last published imbalance level.

violation_hypotheses: A large buy imbalance with a falling indicative price may reveal faster offsetting supply, cancellations or a different auction allocation response; that revision path may be more informative than imbalance sign.

literature_sources.citation: Wu and Jegadeesh (2022), Closing Auctions: Nasdaq versus NYSE, Journal of Financial Economics 143(3), 1120-1139.
literature_sources.supports: Closing-auction imbalance, depth, impact and resiliency differ by market design; a temporary impact component dissipates over subsequent days.

mechanisms.title: Lead-lag price discovery between futures and cash instruments
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Economically linked instruments process common information and liquidity shocks at different speeds; leadership can depend on liquidity, volatility, market hours and shock type.
actors: Liquidity takers choosing among linked venues
constraints_or_rules: Linked contracts share an underlying payoff or basket identity, subject to basis and execution frictions
expected_actions: Trade the faster or cheaper venue first and arbitrage temporary dislocations across linked instruments

observable_signatures.statement: A statistically ordered response of cash, ETF or component prices after a futures move
Short-lived divergence from the contemporaneous linked-instrument relation

phases.trigger: One linked market moves while another remains temporarily stale
phases.expected_response: The lagging instrument catches up or the leading move reverses as the basis closes

phases.trigger: The cross-market basis returns to its normal band
phases.expected_response: The ordered catch-up or leader-reversal response ends as the linked-instrument relation normalizes

alternative_observables.observable: Time-varying leadership score by session and shock type
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether leadership switches across open, continuous session and high-volatility states instead of assuming a permanent leader.

violation_hypotheses: When the usual leader fails to transmit, the move may be a venue-specific liquidity shock; reversal in the apparent leader can be a separate candidate from catch-up in the laggard.

literature_sources.citation: Chan (1992), A Further Analysis of the Lead-Lag Relationship between the Cash Market and Stock Index Futures Market, Review of Financial Studies 5(1), 123-152.
literature_sources.supports: Intraday index futures lead cash indexes and components more strongly for market-wide movements in the studied sample.

mechanisms.title: Recurring intraday return and liquidity patterns at clock time
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Returns, order imbalance, volume, volatility and spreads can recur at the same intraday interval across days even when no single compelled actor is identified.
expected_actions: Repeated execution and liquidity patterns recur at matching clock intervals across sessions

observable_signatures.statement: Cross-sectional return continuation at half-hour intervals separated by exact multiples of a trading day
Recurring volume, imbalance, volatility or spread state at the same intraday interval

phases.trigger: A clock interval with a documented recurring flow pattern approaches
phases.expected_response: Liquidity and order placement adjust before the interval if participants anticipate the recurring flow

phases.trigger: The matching intraday interval begins
phases.expected_response: Return or liquidity state shows continuation related to prior same-time observations

alternative_observables.observable: Execution-cost or spread recurrence at matching clock intervals
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether the repeatable object is liquidity or execution cost rather than directional return.

violation_hypotheses: A return pattern that disappears while the liquidity pattern remains may indicate that anticipation has moved the opportunity from price direction to execution timing.

literature_sources.citation: Heston, Korajczyk and Sadka (2010), Intraday Patterns in the Cross-Section of Stock Returns, Journal of Finance 65(4), 1369-1407.
literature_sources.supports: Return continuation and liquidity variables recur at half-hour intervals that are exact multiples of a trading day; sub-hour reversal is linked to temporary liquidity imbalance.

mechanisms.title: Benchmark-driven index rebalancing
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Index additions, deletions and weight changes induce benchmark-linked trading, while anticipatory arbitrage and changing implementation practice can move pressure before the effective close or reduce it over time.
constraints_or_rules: Funds seek to track announced benchmark composition and weights around an effective date
expected_actions: Buy additions or weight increases and sell deletions or weight decreases, often near the benchmark close

observable_signatures.statement: Concentrated effective-date closing-auction flow aligned with benchmark weight changes
Price adjustment before the effective date as arbitrageurs anticipate benchmark demand

phases.trigger: An index change is announced before its effective date
phases.expected_response: Part of expected benchmark pressure moves into the announcement-to-effective window

phases.trigger: The effective-date closing auction executes
phases.expected_response: Benchmark-aligned flow concentrates in affected securities relative to available auction liquidity

phases.trigger: Mandatory benchmark trading completes
phases.expected_response: Any temporary price-pressure component can reverse after the effective date

alternative_observables.observable: Timing shift from effective close to pre-effective trading
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether the remaining opportunity is anticipation timing or auction liquidity rather than the historical close-to-close index effect.

violation_hypotheses: A weak effective-date return despite large benchmark demand may indicate anticipation and improved liquidity provision; pressure may have migrated to earlier sessions or auction-depth variables.

literature_sources.citation: Pavlova and Sikorskaya (2023), Benchmarking Intensity, Review of Financial Studies 36(3), 859-903.
literature_sources.supports: Benchmark additions and deletions induce passive and active fund rebalancing and cross-sectional price pressure related to benchmarking intensity.

literature_sources.citation: Greenwood and Sammon (2025), The Disappearing Index Effect, Journal of Finance 80(2), 657-698.
literature_sources.supports: The abnormal return around major index additions and deletions declined materially over time, motivating anticipation and adaptation hypotheses.

mechanisms.title: Perpetual-futures funding and forced liquidation feedback
mechanisms.mechanism_summary: Periodic funding transfers anchor perpetual futures to spot, while leveraged positions can be forcibly liquidated when maintenance margin is breached, creating urgent flow and cross-market feedback.
constraints_or_rules: Funding is exchanged at scheduled intervals according to contract rules
Positions breaching maintenance margin are forcibly reduced or closed
expected_actions: Adjust basis positions near funding or submit urgent liquidation flow after margin breaches

observable_signatures.statement: Perpetual-spot basis and positioning change around funding timestamps
Aggressive forced flow, rapid open-interest reduction and volatility spike after liquidation thresholds are crossed

phases.trigger: A funding timestamp approaches with an extreme basis or funding rate
phases.expected_response: Basis and hedge positions adjust before the payment snapshot

phases.trigger: A leveraged price move breaches clustered maintenance-margin thresholds
phases.expected_response: Forced liquidation flow reinforces the move and reduces open interest

phases.trigger: Forced liquidation flow subsides after a large open-interest reduction
phases.expected_response: Urgent flow disappears and an overshoot or basis dislocation can partially reverse

alternative_observables.observable: Open-interest change and perpetual-spot basis rather than exchange-reported liquidation notional
alternative_observables.hypothesis_prompt: Test whether joint basis compression and open-interest collapse identify the end of forced flow more reliably than a liquidation print alone.

violation_hypotheses: A large price move without open-interest contraction may be voluntary directional flow rather than liquidation; a price move with open-interest collapse but no continuation may mark immediate absorption.

literature_sources.citation: Cheng, Deng, Wang and Yu (2021), Liquidation, Leverage and Optimal Margin in Bitcoin Futures Markets, arXiv:2102.04591v1 [q-fin.TR].
literature_sources.supports: Forced liquidations are economically substantial in BitMEX perpetual futures and execute aggressively at high leverage.

literature_sources.citation: He et al. (2022), Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures.
literature_sources.supports: Periodic funding transfers are the contract mechanism used to anchor perpetual futures to their target spot value.
